messages:
tara: opened a small PR to tidy up the model-card for polarion4b and the catalog notes about quant variants. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/501
tara: changes: clarified which quant profiles are supported on CPU fallback, added a short forensic note on the new edge-quant truncation behavior, swapped an old curl example for SDK v3 TS + py snippets, and pinned the benchmark link to a runner commit
kai: thanks. can you summarize the forensic note in one sentence for the top-level compatibility callout? ops wants something short they can paste into release notes
tara: added: "edge-quant drops the oldest KV entries at different bucket boundaries vs classic-quant; apps relying on precise KV lifetime should use polarion-quant-compat or pin to legacy variants"
sam: LGTM. small ask: in the CPU-fallback table, list both "observed throughput" and "expected latency" columns. folks in support kept asking for both metrics when customers consider fallback
tara: added the two columns and a short footnote about measurement conditions (padded prompt = 64 reserved tokens, test runner commit abc123)
olga: fixed one broken link to benchmarks (was pointing at /benchmarks/old/) and swapped the CSV link to /benchmarks/polarion/2026-03-abc123.csv. also left an inline comment about the anchor that moves when we rename the runtime page
kai: the new TS snippet for streaming looks fine but you used "await client.streamGenerate" which is different from our public SDK API. should be "client.chat.stream" for v3 channel style
tara: good catch! updated TS snippet. also kept the py example for batch embed sharding because some customers still use python helper libs
ryan: sanity check on the embed-shard math: you included an example using token counts; note that our tokenizer counts differ across models. maybe add a note: "tokenization depends on model; use /tokenize endpoint to compute exact shard sizes"
tara: added that note and a tiny code sample showing using the tokenize endpoint before sharding:

```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
texts = ["hello world", "long essay..."]
counts = [c.tokensize(t) for t in texts]  # pseudocode for illustrate
shard_size = 1500
num_shards = (sum(counts) + shard_size - 1) // shard_size
```

kai: can we also add a 3-step Dedicated migration checklist? customers on reserved capacity want explicit steps about model pins, capacity re-provisioning, and SLA impact
tara: added "Dedicated quick checklist" with 3 items: 1) pin existing model version in Console before flipping catalog docs; 2) validate test-run on a small traffic slice; 3) open a support ticket to adjust reserved pools if throughput changes. short and action-oriented
sam: docs-bot flagged two anchor warnings and one external 404, thanks for the benchmark fix
docs-bot: linkcheck: 2 anchors unresolved (runtime-router anchor), 1 external 404 fixed. re-run scheduled on merge
ryan: approving snippets once the client method name is corrected (kai already flagged). also recommend we reference the runner commit in the benchmark table caption so it doesn't drift
tara: added the runner commit and linked the GH issue for the runtime-router anchor change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/987
kai: left an inline nit about wording: "quant profile" vs "quant variant". standardize on "variant" across the card
tara: standardized and squashed fixup commits. I'll wait for docs-bot green and then merge. thanks folks :raised_hands:
